name: Probability and Statistics for Computing
description: Reasoning under uncertainty: probability, random variables and distributions, expectation and variance, estimation and hypothesis testing, and randomised algorithms and Markov chains.

topics.name: Foundations of Probability
topics.summary: Sample spaces, events and the axioms everything else follows from.

subtopics.name: Sample Spaces and Events
subtopics.summary: Outcomes, events, the probability axioms and counting-based probability.

objectives.text: Define a sample space and event for a described experiment
Apply the probability axioms to compute the probability of a compound event
Compute a probability using combinatorial counting

subtopics.name: Conditional Probability and Independence
subtopics.summary: Conditioning, the multiplication rule, and what independence really means.

objectives.text: Compute a conditional probability from a joint distribution
Test two events for independence
Apply the law of total probability to a partitioned sample space

subtopics.name: Bayes' Theorem
subtopics.summary: Inverting conditional probabilities, and the base rate fallacy.

objectives.text: Apply Bayes' theorem to update a probability given evidence
Explain the base rate fallacy with a diagnostic testing example
Compute a posterior probability for a spam classification scenario

topics.name: Random Variables
topics.summary: Attaching numbers to outcomes so they can be summarised and combined.

subtopics.name: Discrete Random Variables
subtopics.summary: Probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions and their properties.

objectives.text: Construct a probability mass function for a described experiment
Compute a cumulative distribution function from a pmf
Determine the probability of a range of values from a distribution

subtopics.name: Expectation and Variance
subtopics.summary: The mean, variance, standard deviation, and linearity of expectation.

objectives.text: Compute the expectation and variance of a discrete random variable
Apply linearity of expectation to a sum of dependent variables
Explain what variance measures and why standard deviation is often preferred

subtopics.name: Continuous Random Variables
subtopics.summary: Probability density functions, integration and the normal distribution.

objectives.text: Compute a probability from a probability density function by integration
Standardise a normal variable and use standard normal tables
Explain why the probability of any single value is zero for a continuous variable

topics.name: Common Distributions
topics.summary: The standard models, and recognising which one a situation calls for.

subtopics.name: Bernoulli, Binomial and Geometric
subtopics.summary: Repeated trials, counts of successes and waiting times.

objectives.text: Compute binomial probabilities for a stated number of trials
Identify when a geometric distribution models a waiting time
State the mean and variance of the binomial and geometric distributions

subtopics.name: Poisson and Exponential
subtopics.summary: Rare events in an interval, and the time between them.

objectives.text: Model arrivals in an interval using a Poisson distribution
Compute exponential probabilities for inter-arrival times
Explain the memoryless property of the exponential distribution

subtopics.name: The Normal Distribution and the Central Limit Theorem
subtopics.summary: Why sums of many effects look normal, regardless of their own distribution.

objectives.text: State the central limit theorem and its conditions
Apply the CLT to approximate the distribution of a sample mean
Use a normal approximation to a binomial distribution

topics.name: Statistical Inference
topics.summary: Drawing conclusions about a population from a sample, with quantified uncertainty.

subtopics.name: Point and Interval Estimation
subtopics.summary: Estimators, bias, standard error and confidence intervals.

objectives.text: Compute a point estimate and its standard error from sample data
Construct a confidence interval for a population mean
State correctly what a 95% confidence interval does and does not mean

subtopics.name: Hypothesis Testing
subtopics.summary: Null and alternative hypotheses, p-values, significance and errors.

objectives.text: Formulate null and alternative hypotheses for a stated question
Compute a test statistic and interpret the resulting p-value
Distinguish Type I from Type II error and relate them to significance and power

subtopics.name: Experiments and Regression
subtopics.summary: Comparing systems fairly, and fitting a linear relationship.

objectives.text: Design a fair experiment to compare two algorithms empirically
Fit and interpret a simple linear regression
Explain why correlation does not establish causation

topics.name: Randomness in Algorithms
topics.summary: Using randomness deliberately to get simpler or faster algorithms.

subtopics.name: Randomised Algorithms
subtopics.summary: Las Vegas and Monte Carlo algorithms and expected running time.

objectives.text: Distinguish a Las Vegas from a Monte Carlo algorithm
Analyse the expected running time of randomised quicksort
Explain why randomisation defeats adversarial worst-case inputs

subtopics.name: Hashing and Concentration Bounds
subtopics.summary: Universal hashing, collisions, and bounding deviation from the mean.

objectives.text: Compute the expected number of collisions in a hash table
Apply Markov's or Chebyshev's inequality to bound a tail probability
Explain the birthday paradox and its relevance to hashing

subtopics.name: Markov Chains
subtopics.summary: State transitions with no memory, and long-run behaviour.

objectives.text: Construct a transition matrix for a described Markov process
Compute the state distribution after n steps
Determine a stationary distribution and interpret it

topics.name: Working with Data
topics.summary: Summarising and visualising data honestly before modelling it.

subtopics.name: Descriptive Statistics
subtopics.summary: Measures of centre and spread, quartiles and outliers.

objectives.text: Compute mean, median, mode, variance and interquartile range from data
Identify outliers using a stated criterion
Explain when the median is a better summary than the mean

subtopics.name: Summarising and Visualising Data
subtopics.summary: Histograms, box plots and scatter plots, and misleading presentation.

objectives.text: Choose an appropriate plot for a stated data type and question
Interpret a histogram's shape in terms of the underlying distribution
Identify a misleading feature in a presented chart

subtopics.name: Sampling and Bias
subtopics.summary: Representative samples, sampling methods and the biases that invalidate conclusions.

objectives.text: Distinguish random, stratified and convenience sampling
Identify a source of sampling bias in a described study
Explain how sample size affects the precision of an estimate

sources.title: International undergraduate consensus core (MIT, Cambridge, Imperial, Berkeley)
